_note: OUR mapping from benchmark names as papers write them to where the artifact lives. Authored, like DOMAIN_FAMILIES: the names are data-derived (the extracted `datasets` field), the locations are ours and are marked as such in the interface. Every hf/gh id is checked against the Hub / GitHub API by `python3 -m icml.resources --registry`; an id that fails the check carries ok:false and shows no link. Matching is by taxonomy.dataset_key over name + aliases. not_a_dataset lists model names the extractor files under datasets; they never become benchmark chips with links. `id` is the benchmark's stable key (owner, 2026-10-02): a slug of its published name, assigned once and never reused. A benchmark is its published product name: aliases are spelling variants or forms the benchmark itself publishes; a differently named product (a subset, a version, a year) is its own entry, and a bare name is left unmapped so it is counted as written. Entries split out on 2026-10-02 carry no location yet.
